newsitem.title: USA: Virginia Power Surry 1 power plant trips off.
newsitem.headline: Virginia Power Surry 1 power plant trips off.

text.p: Virginia Power Co's 781 megawatt (MW) Surry 1 nuclear power plant was manually tripped due to problems with the reactor's coolant system, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday.
The NRC's daily plant status report said the unit was shut when pressure in the rector's coolant system dropped following a loss of electrical power to the unit's pressurizer heaters.
The unit, which was operating at full capacity early Wednesday, is currently listed as being in "hot shutdown," which typically indicates a prompt restart is expected.
The company was not immediately available for comment on the outage.
The adjacent nuclear unit, Surry 2, tripped off line Tuesday after losing power in its electrical hydraulic control system.
Virginia Power said the Surry 2 plant, also rated at 781 MW, likely would be restarted by the weekend.
Surry units 1 and 2 are at Virginia Power's Gravel Neck, Va., nuclear generating station.
Virginia Power is a subsidiary of Dominion Resources.
